record.paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
record.original_question: In the same real compact-set sumset setting, what conditions on the tail sets R_z guarantee that S is an M-Cantorval (a perfect set whose every gap is accumulated on both sides by infinitely many intervals and gaps), an L-Cantorval (every gap has an interval adjacent on the right and is accumulated on the left by infinitely many intervals and gaps), or an R-Cantorval (the left-right reversed version)?

evidence.quote:
3. Under what conditions on the tail Rz will this set be an M-Cantorval? An
L or R Cantorval?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers with $a_n \to 0$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n < \infty$. Define the achievement set (or subsum set)
$$S = S(a) = \Big\{ \sum_{n \in A} a_n : A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R},$$
and for each integer $z \ge 0$ define the tail set
$$R_z = \Big\{ \sum_{n \in A} a_n : A \subseteq \{z+1, z+2, \dots\} \Big\}.$$
A nonempty perfect compact subset $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is called a Cantorval if it is the closure of its interior and yet both endpoints of every nontrivial component interval are accumulation points of trivial components (singletons). More specifically:
- $C$ is an $M$-Cantorval if every gap (i.e., bounded connected component of the complement of $C$ inside the convex hull of $C$) is accumulated on both sides by infinitely many component intervals of $C$ and by infinitely many gaps.
- $C$ is an $L$-Cantorval if every gap has a component interval of $C$ adjacent to it on the right while being accumulated on the left by infinitely many component intervals and infinitely many gaps.
- $C$ is an $R$-Cantorval if it is the mirror image (under $x \mapsto -x$) of an $L$-Cantorval.

It is known that $S$ is always either a finite union of closed intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval (of one of the three types above). 

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the family of tail sets $\{R_z\}_{z\ge 0}$ that characterize when $S$ is an $M$-Cantorval, an $L$-Cantorval, and an $R$-Cantorval, respectively.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature provides sufficient conditions for the achievement set of certain multigeometric series to be an M-Cantorval, and gives full topological trichotomy theorems, but no general necessary-and-sufficient characterization of M-, L-, or R-Cantorval type in terms of the tail sets $R_z$ appears in available sources. The question is posed as an open problem in surveys on subsums of null sequences, and recent papers (e.g., on multigeometric Cantorvals, 2022–2025) continue to address only special cases.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Trichotomy: subsum set is a finite union of intervals, a Cantor set, or a (symmetric) Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: General trichotomy is known but the fine M/L/R classification via tails is not characterized.

status_evidence.title: The Lebesgue measure of boundaries of multigeometric Cantorvals
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for sets of subsums of special multigeometric series to be M-Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still treats only special families, indicating the general tail-based characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: Conditions for the Difference Set of a Central Cantor Set to be a Cantorval
status_evidence.snippet: Provides conditions for difference sets to be Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations exist in special settings but not a complete tail-based criterion for M/L/R types.
